notes.title: 6/4 SteamInput Hotfix
notes.content: Fixes the SteamInput localization. Actions should now be more human-readable when editing SteamInput controller configurations.

notes.title: 2024 Christmas Update
notes.content:
Happy holidays and merry Christmas!

[h3]New Arena: Present[/h3]
The new map is a small square with 4 holes and a bow on top. Once again, this seasonal map is very good for the "Grappler" tank. Maybe all seasonal arenas will start with "P" and be good for Grappler. Accidental patterns aside, it is a great map for 2-3 tanks that requires constant movement and careful dashing to avoid falling into the holes.

This new map can be unlocked by playing at least one Arena Mode match during the month of December. As always, If you miss it, just change your system clock to December and play a match.

[h3]Bug Fix[/h3]
This update also fixes a bug where AI/CPU tanks would sometimes run off the edge after eliminating an opponent. This was most noticeable in Treasure Mode, but you should also see an improvement in your CPU partners in Survival Mode.

notes.title: 2024 Halloween Update
notes.content:
Happy Halloween!

[h3]New Arena: Pumpkin[/h3]
The new map is a large jack-o-lantern. The map is similar to the "Smile" arena, but much wider and with holes instead of pillars for eyes. These additional holes in it make it a great map for the Grappler tank, and the narrow strips around the mouth and eyes work well for heavy, hard-to-move tanks such as Boulder.

This new map can be unlocked by playing at least one Arena Mode match during the month of October. Sorry this update came out only 3 full days before November! If you miss it and can't wait until October 2025, just change your system clock to October and play a match.

[h3]Seasonal Maps[/h3]
"Pumpkin" is the first of what I hope will be several seasonal maps that can be unlocked around specific holidays. Pumpkin is for Halloween and a "Tree" map is planned for Christmas in December.

notes.title: Easier Cross-Play Between the Demo and Full Game
notes.content:
Recently, Steam made it possible to reinstall a demo after you've purchased the full game. Previously, you had to open up the hidden console on the Steam client and input a specific set of commands. Now, you can just click the "Install Demo" button on the store page. That's a lot easier! Thank you, Steam!



[b]As a reminder, here's how cross-play between the demo and full game works:[/b]
[h2]Is there cross-play between the Demo and Full versions of the game?[/h2]
Yes and no. While the demo and full game are separate on Steam and cannot play together, if you purchase the full game, the full game's content is also added to your demo. Your demo, now identical to the full game, [i]can[/i] join or host games for other demos, allowing you to share the full game's content with your friends.

[h2]If I own the full game, what content can I share in demo games?[/h2]
When selecting tanks, arenas, and game modes, players will only see what they have unlocked. Other players will not have the option to select content from the full game, but you can select it for them.

When playing Campaign Mode, the number of levels depends on the host. If the host owns the full game, players will tackle all 100 levels and bonus levels. If the host does not, then there will only be 30 levels without bonus levels.

[h2]If I own the full game, how can I download the demo again?[/h2]
You can download it from the [url=store.steampowered.com/app/2699030/]demo store page[/url].

[h2]Still Have Questions?[/h2]
Cross-play between the demo and full game have a dedicated [url=steamcommunity.com/app/2475720/discussions/0/4339859086866088649/]Steam discussion[/url]. That is the best place to get the most up-to-date information and ask questions.

notes.title: 6/27 "Clarity Update"
notes.content:
Happy Steam Summer Sale! The June 27th update is a collection of small-to-medium quality of life changes that center around making the game more "clear" to new players. Hence, it is nicknamed the "Clarity Update." This update is not as exciting as new content, but I hope these changes help new players learn the game and help current players become experts.

These changes apply to both the demo and full game.


[h2]Dashing Rework[/h2]
While most of the changes are purely UI, there is one big gameplay change: dashing now slides along walls. Previously, running into a wall would prematurely end a dash. Now, if you hit a wall, you will slide along it until the dash ends normally. [strike]It's like wall running in other games.[/strike] However, if you hit a wall head on, you will still bounce off it. Check it out the before and after below!

[h3]Before[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/5ac6867649e5f6bb451ad4f1c2f7db83cae56e14.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/41a11582a345c3b66f0c0fae7acefa22fe418f0e.gif[/img]

[h3]After[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/2acf2f22a02108f8adb7abaecc33a3bf9cb9d2cb.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/706f143131652a3157ffd6d1c7cee05615843ae3.gif[/img]


[h2]Campaign Mode Improvements[/h2]
Enemy tanks are now color-coded and have a line of sight cone when searching for your tank.

[h3]Color-Coding[/h3]
Enemy tanks in campaign mode are divided into three colors based on their behavior:
[b]Orange:[/b] A tank that does not dash.
[b]Red:[/b] A tank that dashes to avoid edges, making it harder to ring out.
[b]Black:[/b] The black belt of Sumo Tanks. It both dashes to avoid edges and to ram players out of the arena.

[h3]Line of Sight[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/87da0c1dcfa0732c95cf280bc137551682c19f9e.gif[/img]
In the early campaign levels, there are many tanks that will not attack until they see you. These "scanning" tanks now have a cone that shows where they are currently looking, helping you avoid their line of sight and sneak up behind them. However, beware, once you hit these tanks they will notice you.


[h2]Controller Numbering[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/5ca821d15fc06e6d54c56498b0784f517ae66f54.png[/img]
Controllers are now numbered, and this number appears both on menu cursors and above player-controlled (i.e., not CPU, not online) tanks before a match starts. Some players reported losing track of themselves in-game or in-menus when playing with 4+ people. More work will be done to prevent that, but this is a first step to address the issue in the short-term. In menus, numbering allow players to know which cursor is theirs. In game, The numbering and new indicator above human-controlled tanks helps players quickly see where they are.


[h2]Tank Selection Improvements[/h2]
There are now tooltips to describe each tank and what "Simplify Controls" does, and there is a new animation once you lock in your choice.

[h3]Tooltips[/h3]
Ever want to know what a tank does without trying it out? When you're selecting your tank, you can now hover over it to see an explanation of what makes it special. Likewise, hovering over "Simplify Controls" now shows an explanation of what it does (force your tank to always shoots in the direction it is facing). I hope these small changes empower players to setup their tanks in the way that works best and is the most fun for them.

[h3]New "Ready" Graphic[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/014dc7a1ba401e9a3c04fc7c8d93285db6db3c9e.gif[/img]
Previously, when locking in on the tank select menu, the "player banner" would be greyed out. That wasn't exciting, so there is now a banner that falls over your selection after you press "Ready." This banner is loosely based on the kensho (懸賞) banners that are displayed before real-world sumo matches. In the real world, these banners represent the sponsors that are providing the prize money for the match. They have some really cool designs, so look up "kensho sumo banner" if you're interested!


[h2]Target Improvements: Show Time Limit[/h2]
When breaking targets, it was hard to know how much time you had until the level started. The following changes have been made to fix that:
[list]
[*]On bonus levels in Campaign Mode, the time limit is shown before players ready up.
[*]On target practice levels, the player's best time or the developer's time-to-beat is shown before players ready up.
[/list]

[h2]Smaller Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed the tutorial text blocking the "back to menu" button on some monitors.
[*]Made the lobby join code input larger.
[*]Replaced incorrect shadow texture for the Boulder tank.
[*]Adjusted the Boulder tank's head to make the front and back more distinct.
[*]When adding a player with teams enabled, the new player's team now matches the side it was added on.
[/list]

notes.title: Sharing the Full Game with Demo Players
notes.content:
The 5/18 update to the Sumo Tanks demo includes various bug fixes, a few features from the playtest, and, most importantly, the ability to host the full game for other demo players.

[h2]How can I host the full version of Sumo Tanks for other demo players?[/h2]
When you purchase the full game, the full game's content is also added to your demo, allowing you to share it with other players online. So, once you own the full game, all you need to do is launch the demo and invite players like you normally would. That's it.

If you need to reinstall the demo, please see this steam discussion: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2475720/discussions/0/4339859086866088649/]https://steamcommunity.com/app/2475720/discussions/0/4339859086866088649/[/url].

While progress is synced between "Sumo Tanks" and "Sumo Tanks Demo," they are separate games on Steam and CANNOT play together. Please keep this in mind. If you are playing with friends who only have the demo, launch "Sumo Tanks Demo." If all your friends own the full game, launch "Sumo Tanks."

Until the playtest ends on 5/20, players who have been invited to the playtest can also host the full game for demo players.

[h2]What content is shared?[/h2]
Players can only see the content they have unlocked, but you can select your unlocked tanks, arenas, and modes, even for other players. All tanks, arenas, and modes can be shared this way. The only exception are the levels in Campaign Mode, which are tied to the host. If the host does not own the full game, then you will only play the 30 demo levels. If the host owns the full game, then the full 100 levels will be shared.

If you want to know what sort of content you can unlock in the full game, check out the Release Date announcement where we go over it: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2475720/view/4179980031200718738]https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2475720/view/4179980031200718738[/url]

[h2]New Demo Features[/h2]
Even if you don't own the full game, you will have access to the following new features:
[list]
[*]Teams in Arena Mode
[*]Online join codes, and an option for streamers to hide them
[*]Simplified controls where you always shoot in the direction your tank is facing
[*]Controller rumble when running into another tank or being shot
[/list]
...and the following quality of life improvements:
[list]
[*]Improved dash indicator
[*]The onscreen keyboard no longer requires launching through Steam Big Picture Mode
[*]Online performance improvements
[*]Campaign level re-balancing
[*]Assorted bug fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Playtesting Returns & A Release Date is Announced
notes.content:
[h1]Playtesting is back! This time it is for the full game.[/h1]
[h2]Why have a separate playtest?[/h2]
While the game has been tested as much as possible, it may still have bugs. Playtesting is being run separately to catch any bugs before the full release. If you encounter any bugs, please report them in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2475720/discussions/0/3960413951795906204/]Steam Discussions[/url].

For a stable version of Sumo Tanks, please wait for the full release.

[h2]How to join[/h2]
If you were part of the February playtest, thank you! More importantly, you are already approved for this round of playtesting and can join as soon as the update downloads.

If you missed the February playtest, you can sign up for this round of playtesting on the Steam store page. Once you are approved, you can try out the playtest version. Players will be randomly approved as the playtest becomes more stable.

Sign-ups close the week before Sumo Tanks releases, but you can continue playing until the 20th. As for when Sumo Tanks releases...

[h1]The Full Game[/h1]
[h2]Sumo Tanks releases on May 20th[/h2]
That's this month!

[h1]What's in the full game?[/h1]
The demo currently has 2 game modes, 3 playable tanks, and 4 arenas. The full game has 4 game modes, 8 playable tanks, and 33 arenas! Spoilers ahead...

[h2]New modes[/h2]
If you have played the demo, you have already experienced the PvP Arena Mode and the co-op Campaign Mode. Those modes are still in the full version, but they have expanded, new content! Arena Mode has more arenas and more tanks. Campaign Mode has 70 additional levels, bringing the final total to 100. In addition to this, there are new bonus levels that task you with breaking targets before time runs out. The more targets you break, the more extra lives you earn. If you want to improve your clear time, you can practice these level in [b]Target Practice Mode[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/4ad9d713f871b09c9403d26329e649e59a7a481a.png[/img]

Some playtesters requested an endless version of Campaign Mode, and the new [b]Survival Mode[/b] is just that! Survive waves of enemies to make it to the next arena. If you last long enough, you'll be able to take a breather and purchase upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/b9f1282f4bf0bc3b71434683d27e805543eb8bde.png[/img]

If you want another PvP mode, [b]Treasure Mode[/b] is a king-of-the-hill variant of Arena Mode. Instead of competing to be the last tank standing, players vie for control over treasure spots on the map. The first tank to dig up enough treasure is the winner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/ec98546619adb45c227791119470b3c54d3d7db6.png[/img]

[h2]New Tanks[/h2]
Balanced, Rocket, and Dancer all return for the full game, and they are joined by Grappler, Homing, Laser, Knight, and Boulder.

[h3]Grappler[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/4023b6145e3664a0a3eb9b048b2c29d792567c4f.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/e61c4580d699d88b2a6e5d2d3dd1f6a67780ad04.png[/img][/url]
[b]Grappler[/b] actually appears in a few of the demo levels, but is unplayable [strike]unless you cheat[/strike]. This heavy tank pulls enemies close with its grappling hook and then shoots or dashes into them to send them flying. It is a little tricky, but, once you get the hang of it, you'll have a lot of fun throwing tanks around.

[h3]Homing[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/c100c32f152aaee3bd06333b6facfa24ca34bd69.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/5cfdae2c6a25232b06767037a68f5b14f76ec6f2.png[/img][/url]
[b]Homing[/b] is the most "normal" of the new tanks. It is like Balanced, except its shells follow the nearest enemy tank. If you have trouble aiming, this is the tank for you!

[h3]Laser[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/debde805b358bc317b61a7195e9d117db3f01a92.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/eff1b0347edc6ca82330df53db0dbac2a5bd94b7.png[/img][/url]
[b]Laser[/b] is heavy and its laser doesn't do much damage, but it is relentless. Laser does not need to reload, which means your enemies will be constantly shoved back so long as you have that laser focused on them.

[h3]Knight[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/16ab034ba9df25cea7f1e3b06aa62124fcfe4299.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/9e90658a3291d71c635a79472208e8fbb74d5eb3.png[/img][/url]
[b]Knight[/b] is one of two "melee tanks." It slashes tanks and reflects bullets with its sword. It is very satisfying to send an explosive shell right back at a Rocket tank. Try it out!

[h3]Boulder[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/1f715242628cd03ed895d302843b9eb751120805.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/01460dd52215a302ce685c16baa8e806b73c47d1.png[/img][/url]
[b]Boulder[/b] is the other "melee" tank and, as the name implies, it is HEAVY. Boulder might be slow, but it can explode, sending it flying forward at high speeds. You don't want to be in front of it when that happens. It is probably the most "sumo-like" of all the tanks.


[h2]New Arenas[/h2]
There are too many new arenas to cover here, but there are a few I wanted to highlight.

[h3]Mat[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/0c6e2620869c43d4a6c1bdd225e4dce8eac08fe2.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/cc43876610fe16e1261ecc50988ef7b324f3cdc0.png[/img][/url]
[b]Mat[/b] might be just be a large rectangle, but its openness makes it perfect if you are playing with a full 8 tanks! If you want a more exciting arena...

[h3]Smile[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/7555225ed379f093351585c74eca3aa6c59b66eb.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/74544ce8fa1ba0bf70b1e3991165a70c35a8cb64.png[/img][/url]
A few of the new arenas are goofy, [b]Smile[/b] included. Still, it is a good showcase of what to expect: barriers from pillars and gaps in the arena that Grappler can pull you into.

[h3]Letter H & Variants[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/1f23131b546da1b1eead34b4b5fd0b2c3c66a1b8.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/9652a71991839abfbda8d738de685b35a392a213.png[/img][/url]    [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/30c8ffe9c1bff5a48df290f0388836e8dab959e9.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/fade4a7390d1b48b24b1b444c0aee32006a302a3.png[/img][/url]    [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/f99c48074614075b18f6a90a94dae8c292231567.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/03a5b8ec1a336f3b454cac4defe567590c9a1967.png[/img][/url]    [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/86025419bc743dba53d75b48eec9bbfc1d3c88bc.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/f154fffd52bdbff33859c18d9f184021f2ec15a5.png[/img][/url]
Some of the new arenas belong to a "family." The largest of these family is the [b]Letter H[/b] arenas. They might look similar, but the obstacles and asymmetry make them play very differently!

[h2]Unlocks[/h2]
As you play the game, especially campaign mode, you will naturally complete challenges that unlock these new tanks, modes, and arenas. If you want to speed things up, take a look at all the unlocks and their requirements on the main menu!

[h2]Minor Quality of Life Updates[/h2]
There are also several minor quality of life changes that will be added in the next demo update. These include:
[list]
[*]Rumble.
[*]Online lobby join codes.
[*]Kicking players from multiplayer.
[*]Smoke trails behind rockets.
[*]An on-screen keyboard that works without Big Picture Mode.
[*]Improved dash indicator.
[*]Campaign progress tracking on the main menu.
[*]Campaign rebalancing.
[*]Bug fixes.
[/list]
[h1]FAQ[/h1]
[h2]Will my progress carry over to the full game?[/h2]
Yes. However, if you play the demo after the playtest, your progress may be reset.

[h2]Does the playtest have online?[/h2]
Yes! However, you can only play with other people who have the playtest. You cannot join a demo game from the playtest and vice versa. However, if some experimental development goes well, this may be possible in the next few weeks.

[h2]What's next?[/h2]
The usual: bug fixes, balancing, and quality of life changes.

There are a few other larger updates in development:
[list]
[*]If develop goes well, the demo and full version (including the playtest) of Sumo Tanks will be able to play together online. I am particularly excited for this because it means only 1 player (the host) would have to own the full game. The rest can play for free! Hopefully development goes well. Stay tuned!
[*]An option for simplified controls will be added soon. These controls will always make the tank face in the direction it is turned, greatly helping people who have difficulty aiming and moving at the same time.
[*]An option to hide the lobby join code so that streamers don't have to worry about viewers barging into their games uninvited.
[/list]

notes.title: 2/7 Demo Quality of Life Update
notes.content:
The February 7th update includes many small changes aimed at improving the experience for new and returning players. Thank you to everyone who has played the demo at Next Fest and given feedback! A lot of these changes are for y'all.

[h1]Rebalancing Tanks[/h1]
One consistent area of feedback was "Dancer is too weak and Rocket is too strong." Dancer has been slightly buffed and Rocket has been nerfed.

[h2]Weight Changes[/h2]
Every tank has a weight assigned to it that determines how far it travels after being hit or rammed. Dancer's weight has been increased and Rocket's has been decreased. The result is that it is easier for Dancer to recover from being hit and Rocket is easier to knock out of the arena.

[h2]Explosion Duration Reduced[/h2]
Previously, explosions would damage tanks even if only a little smoke was on screen. This led to weird behavior where it looked like tanks were knocked back by nothing. Explosions now only damage tanks immediately after they explode. This slightly nerfs Rocket.

[h2]Shell Size Increase[/h2]
Shells are now 15% larger. This may sound like a small change, but it makes it noticeably easier to aim and to shoot down incoming shells. This change indirectly nerfs Rocket, since its signature rocket shell is easier to shoot down now.

[h1]Preventing AI Stalemates[/h1]
Previously, when 2 AI would face off in Arena Mode, they would often end up in an unending stalemate, forcing the player pause and take over one of the tanks or exit to the main menu. There have been several changes to the Arena Mode AI that now prevent stalemates. The two most notable changes are that AIs now move around the arena more and vary the angle of their shots. The end result is that the AI now takes risks that break stalemates.

That all being said, AI matches on certain maps can sometimes still take awhile to finish. The new behavior makes them more entertaining to watch and they [i]will[/i] end, but future updates will be improving this further.

[h1]Randomized Arena Starting Point[/h1]
Previously, tanks would start in the same location every round. Now, the starting points change every round. This should bring more variety to matches and prevent one player from having an unfair starting advantage.

[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
There are several more minor changes:
[list]
[*]A new campaign level has been added as an easier match between the 2nd and old 3rd matches. This brings the total number of levels in the demo to an even 30.
[*]Further Campaign Mode rebalancing to reduce difficulty spikes.
[*]Pool now has smaller walls, making it easier to knock tanks out.
[*]The preview for Pillar is now smaller, better reflecting the actual size of the arena.
[*]After purchasing the final upgrade in the campaign, an indicator now appears, telling you to drive off.
[*]Control mapping nickname lengths have been increased from 5 characters to 7. This is the name that displays when a control is selected (e.g., "KB+M" for keyboard and mouse).
[*]Steam avatars now appear next to the cursors for online players.
[*]The controls for online players are now displayed as "Online" instead of "Network."
[*]Fixed an intermittent crash when disconnecting an in-use controller while playing online.
[*]Fixed an online desync that occurred if a player joined during upgrade selection after a tank had been replaced with a CPU.
[/list]

notes.title: Online Multiplayer Added to the Demo!
notes.content:
After last week's playtest, online multiplayer has been added to the Sumo Tanks demo. Thank you to all the playtesters who gave feedback and helped catch bugs! Thanks to them, everyone can now enjoy online multiplayer with their friends.

[h1]How to access online multiplayer[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/049e05d1803a6ba72be7e275017150bf9590d420.png[/img]
There is a new "Online" sidebar that can be accessed [i]anywhere[/i] at [i]anytime[/i]. To invite a friend to join you, just open the sidebar, click the plus, and select them. Friends can also join you through Steam via the normal "Join Game" option on the friends list.

This sidebar can be toggled open and closed by clicking it in the top right, pressing tab, or by clicking "Online" on the main menu.

notes.title: Public Demo Online Playtest
notes.content:
Online for Sumo Tanks is here! Anyone can try it out by signing up for the playtest on the Steam store page. Until February 4th, the playtest will be open to everyone. After that, the playtest will end and online will be added to the proper Sumo Tanks demo.

[h2]How can I play online?[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/049e05d1803a6ba72be7e275017150bf9590d420.png[/img]
There is a new "Online" dropdown in the top right of the screen. Clicking the dropdown or pressing tab will open it, and you'll be able to invite friends. Alternatively, your friends can join you directly from Steam without an invite. One player will be the "host" for all others. If the "host" disconnects, all other players will disconnect and return to the title screen.

Players can join at any point: on the main menu, selecting upgrades, or playing a match, it doesn't matter. Once they connect, they can watch the current game. If you pause, they can even take over a tank and join you!

[h2]Why have a separate playtest? Why not just update the demo?[/h2]
Online has been tested as much as possible, but it may still have bugs. So, the playtest is being run separately to catch any bugs before adding online to the demo. If you encounter any bugs, please report them in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2475720/discussions/0/3960413951795906204/]Steam Discussions[/url].

For a stable version of Sumo Tanks, please play the demo or wait until February 5th for online to be added.

[h2]Is this a playtest for the full game?[/h2]
No. This is a playtest for the [b]DEMO[/b] with online. The available tanks, levels, and arenas are identical to the demo. The only difference is that you can now play online.

[h2]What happens to the playtest after it closes?[/h2]
Online and any feedback will be added to the demo, and you will unable to launch the playtest from Steam. However, there will be another playtest for the full game at a later date. If you sign up for this playtest, you will be able to join the full playtest when it releases.

notes.title: 1/24 Demo Update: New & Rebalanced Content
notes.content:
Ahead of Next Fest, the Sumo Tanks Demo has been expanded with new content and rebalanced for new players and tighter controls.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[h2]New Arena: Parthenon[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/7ed3878fafc4dbe1b5e8485e51428fed1dd319b3.png[/img]
Parthenon is a large arena broken up by several pillars. While the pillars provide cover not found in the Pool and (ironically) Pillar maps, they are too small to camp behind, unlike the walls in Hallway. Matches in this arena involve weaving in and out of cover while closing in for the kill.

[h2]Expanded & Rebalanced Campaign[/h2]
14 levels have been added to the demo campaign, almost doubling it to 29 levels! The difficulty of the previous campaign was a problem for many new players, so special attention has been given to rebalancing existing levels and fixing the difficulty curve. If you got stuck last time, give the new demo campaign a shot!

[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
[h2]CPU Difficulties[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/f11dacf1e5d045327d1168b6dbc9bb1595a52b25.png[/img]
Similar to the campaign, CPUs have been rebalanced with the addition of a difficulty setting. When selecting "CPU" for a tank, you now have the option to set a difficulty from Easy to Expert. The better the CPU, the more aggressive it is and the better it is at staying in the arena.

If you just want to mess around, there is a "Practice" option. Practice CPUs will try to stay in the arena but will not shoot at you. Also, yes, you can add "Expert" CPUs to your team in Campaign Mode.

[h2]Physics Rework[/h2]
There are two major changes to physics:

The first and most obvious is that tanks have much tighter controls and no longer drive like they're on ice. Turning and acceleration is faster, and tanks drift less at high speeds. Overall, the controls are much more responsive.

The second change is that shooting no longer has recoil. Previously, shooting would push your tank in the opposite direction of the shot. While this could be used to cancel out velocity without turning (especially for the Dancer tank), it often just resulted in players shooting themselves out of the arena. Thank you to everyone who gave feedback! You can now shoot near the edge with no consequences.

[h2]Control Changes[/h2]
Keeping with the theme of twos, there are two changes to controls.

Reversing has been removed. Since tanks turn fast now, there is no need to reverse.

The second change is more technical. The short version of it is that controller configurations are now bundled with the game and have changed to accommodate a new "multiplayer" button (foreshadowing online playtesting in a future update). Your controls should automatically update. However, if you experience any problems, you can rebind the controls through Steam Input or by accessing the Controls Options from the main menu:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44614095/76fca27c9530f5710b62fa3935fa9e282df80cc9.png[/img]

[h1]The Future[/h1]
Multiplayer for the demo is coming soon. Internal testing is just finishing and the last bugs are being squashed before the public playtest. More details to come in the next few days. In the meantime, if you have any issues or feedback, feel free to reach out through the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2475720/discussions/]Steam community[/url]!
